questions.question_text: Prevalence of hallucinatory experiences in healthy British respondents from community samples is estimated to be around
questions.explanation:
ONS 2000 Psychiatric morbidity survey obtained a nationally representative sample of 8580 adults aged 16-74 years living in private

questions.question_text:
Prevalence of mental health problems in community surveys is always higher than the prevalence in clinical samples. Which of the following
can explain this?

options.text: Clinical sample surveys underestimate true rates
Di�erence in male and female distribution of illnesses
Existence of diagnostic �lters along the pathway of care

correct_answer.text: Existence of diagnostic �lters along the pathway of care

questions.explanation:
Pathways to care - also called the �lter model - was developed by Goldberg and Huxley, to account for how mental illness interacts with the
healthcare system.  
Five levels of mental illness occurrence were described: The community, the primary care attendees, the diagnosed primary care attendees
(in whom the mental illness has been recognised), the level of psychiatrist and that at the level of psychiatric inpatient care.  
Four �lters explain the decreasing numbers of cases when going from the general population to inpatient psychiatric care 1. At the level of
the patient himself or herself (recognition) 2. At the level of the general practitioner (recognition, decision to treat, decision to refer), 3. At the
outpatient level of the mental healthcare system and 4. At the inpatient admission level. This explains the nature of hurdles one must cross
before being picked up by services; this model explains why community studies show higher rates than clinic-based studies.

questions.question_text: Choose the most likely statement regarding prevention strategies.

options.text: Intervention aimed at high risk individuals is the best approach to help those individuals, but population bene�ts are best achieved with
Secondary prevention is meant to reduce the incidence of the disease by preventing the development of new cases.
Indicated preventive intervention is an intervention targeted to members of a population with higher than average risk factor
The goal of primary prevention to reduce the total number of existing cases by more rapid e�ective intervention which shortens the
Selective preventive intervention is targeted to an entire population.

questions.explanation:
Universal preventive intervention is targeted to an entire population. Selective preventive intervention is an intervention targeted to
members of a population with higher than average risk factors. Indicated preventive intervention is an intervention targeted to members of
a population with subsyndromal symptoms of a disorder (or diagnosed with another associated disorder). Primary prevention is meant to
reduce the incidence of the disease by preventing the development of new cases. The goal of secondary prevention is to reduce the total
number of existing cases by more rapid, e�ective intervention, which shortens the duration of illness.

questions.question_text: Tertiary prevention involves

options.text: Reducing handicap and disabilities that result from diseases
Reducing the incidence of the diseases
Early identi�cation and prompt treatment of illness
Reduction of risk factors and blocking modes of disease transmission

correct_answer.text: Reducing handicap and disabilities that result from diseases

questions.explanation:
Tertiary prevention involves the reduction in the prevalence of residual defects or disabilities that are consequences of the illness. It may not
be possible to eliminate the sequel of the illness fully, but the goal of tertiary prevention is for individuals to reach their highest level of
functioning. In the case of schizophrenia, tertiary prevention is rehabilitation. Relapse prevention is also a form of tertiary prevention.

questions.question_text: Which one among the following is NOT an example of a statutory obligation to disclose information to a third party in the public interest?
questions.explanation:

In other words, from the legal perspective, it is in the public interest for patients to be able to trust their doctors to maintain con�dentiality.
The issue thereof when it is lawful and when not lawful for a doctor to breach con�dentiality is often a question of balancing public interests.
Doctors may be obliged to disclose information to a third partying the public interest and examples are statutory obligations in relation to
relation to communicable diseases, certain controlled drugs, un�tness to drive, suspicion of child abuse or by order of a court and when
there is evidence of a major crime.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true with regard to Rose's 'Prevention Paradox'?

options.text: An intervention aimed at high risk individuals is the best approach to help the population
An intervention aimed at high risk individuals is the best approach to help those individuals, but population wide bene�ts are best
All universal prevention approaches are less cost e�ective than high risk targeted strategies
Primary prevention cannot be achieved in a dynamically ill population
A universal intervention is the best approach to help the individuals at a high risk of a disease

questions.explanation:
In his seminal paper entitled 'Sick individuals and Sick populations', Geo�rey Rose explained the Prevention Paradox he initially put forward
in 1981 using Framingham epidemiological data for coronary disease. Consider cholesterol reduction to prevent myocardial infarctions: a
majority of cases of coronary disease come from a population at low or moderate cholesterol levels, and only a minority of cases come from
the high-risk population. This is because the number of people at high risk is small. Similarly while advanced maternal age is a risk factor for
Down's syndrome, most cases of Down Syndrome are born to younger, low-risk mothers (this is true at least in populations where most
women have children at a younger age). This situation exposes the myth of equating high-risk populations with making up the majority of
the disease burden. This produces a paradoxical disadvantage when implementing universal prevention programmes, as majority of
individuals undergoing universal programmes will have unfavourable cost/e�ect ratio even though at a population level, universal
preventions o�er the maximum bene�t

questions.question_text: Which of the following interventions have been evaluated for early intervention of schizophrenia?

options.text: Use of CBT and supportive therapy

questions.explanation:
CBT may have a role in reducing progression from at risk state to full blown schizophrenia as suggested by EDIE trial (Morrison, 2004). The
SoCRATES study (Study of Cognitive Reality Alignment Therapy in Early Schizophrenia) compared CBT with supportive counselling for a �rst-
or second-episode of schizophrenia wherein at 18-month follow-up (Tarrier et al., 2004), the addition of both CBT and supportive counselling
showed a signi�cant improvement. PRIME study used olanzapine in a low dose to prevent progression with favourable results though it is
not a powerful data to be generalised. EPPIC from Melbourne (McGorry et al) reported that a combination of CBT and risperidone could
reduce the conversion rate at 6 months; though longer follow-up suggested that a delay not prevention e�ect was possible. Warner
reappraised the results of EPPIC report and found out that even one additional case of schizophrenia would have nulli�ed the much glori�ed
results. The Lambeth Early Onset (LEO) study compared specialised care (low dose atypical anti-psychotics, CBT using manualised protocols,
family counselling and vocational strategies) based on a model of assertive outreach with standard care. The remission rates were lower
with specialised care.
